English: Ditch Perimeter
A shallow ditch hastily dug around the castle, offering minimal defense but deterring the most basic assaults.
Earthen Trench
A deeper earthwork trench, laboriously excavated, making it more difficult for enemies to approach the walls.
Dry Moat
A fully dug moat encircling the stronghold, dry but wide enough to impede attackers and siege equipment.
Palisaded Moat
A dry moat reinforced with a wooden palisade, effectively deterring ladders and scaling attempts.
Water-Filled Moat
A deep moat filled with water, sourced from a nearby river or diverted stream, providing exceptional protection against sappers and siege towers.
Wide Moat
A greatly widened moat, making the crossing of siege bridges and ladders nearly impossible without specialized equipment.
Double Moat
A formidable defense: two concentric moats, one dry and one water-filled, creating a deadly obstacle for any attacker.
Stone-Lined Moat
A moat lined with stone, preventing collapse and making sapping or draining extremely difficult.
Bridged Moat
Fortified drawbridges and causeways over the moat, allowing defenders to control all access points with deadly precision.
Fortified Moat
The ultimate defensive moat: broad, deep, stone-lined, with multiple drawbridges, machicolations, and fortified gatehouses, virtually impervious to all but the most determined sieges.
